text:
morgan: Heads up — PR 7821 (alloc-scheduler-refactor) is queued to merge in ~1h. CI bench shows an unexpected tail latency bump on the long-seq workload. Can folks do a quick look? planning to block merge if canary fails.

sam: Can you paste the bench output so we can see the delta?

morgan: Sure — pasted from CI (longseq-64k steady-state):

```
Benchmark suite: longseq-64k
Baseline (main): p50=28ms  p95=120ms  p99=230ms  throughput=850 tok/s  mem_rss=6.1GB
PR7821:          p50=28ms  p95=125ms  p99=256ms  throughput=840 tok/s  mem_rss=6.6GB
Delta: +11% p99, +0.5GB RSS, -1.2% throughput
config: --microbatch=adaptive --sched=heuristic-v2
```

diego: Oof, p99 +11% and RSS +0.5GB is non-trivial. PR touched allocator scoring + pack-until-full logic, right?

morgan: Yep — main changes were: adjust free-list scoring to prefer contiguous blocks, and change packing to "pack-until-full" (to reduce fragmentation). Also bumped microbatch window default 5ms -> 10ms.

elle: Increasing microbatch window can exacerbate tail latency (waiting for batch completion). Can we isolate which change is regressing? e.g. run baseline with new scheduler but old microbatch window, and vice-versa.

ryan: I'll spin a quick canary run on a g4dn cluster and flip the microbatch window first. Give me ~10m.

infra-bot: Canary run started: canary-id=canary-7821-2026-03-17T15:10Z. Workload: 1000 requests (mix: 1k/8k/64k). Logs: https://ci.internal/bench/canary-7821 (automated health checks enabled)

sam: Also capture flamegraphs + alloc profile — should tell if packing increases scan time per alloc.

morgan: Pasted minimal flame top (from profiler attached to the canary):

```
PR7821 flame top (sampled stacks):
30% - alloc::try_alloc (pack loop)
18% - scheduler::select_ready
12% - kv_cache::evict_check
8%  - rpc::send_chunk
```

diego: That 30% in alloc::try_alloc is suspicious — packing likely causes additional scanning/compaction work on hot paths. If the pack loop is O(n) per alloc in some cases, that would explain tail spikes.

elle: My recommendation: hold merge, and either revert pack-until-full or reduce its aggressiveness (e.g., stop after 1 extra scan). We should require canary p99 within 5% of baseline before merging.

ryan: Local canary (with pack-until-full OFF, microbatch=10ms) shows p99 ~= baseline (+2%). With pack-until-full ON, p99 +14%. So microbatch change isn't the only factor.

morgan: Thanks — that suggests packing is the larger signal. Does anyone object to blocking merge and opening a revert? I'll open a revert PR if we decide to roll back pack change.

sam: No objections — hold and investigate. + :thumbsup:

diego: :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Canary results posted: canary-id=canary-7821-2026-03-17T15:20Z. Summary: p50=29ms p95=128ms p99=265ms (baseline p99=230ms) -> Auto-health-check: FAILED (tail latency increased >10%). Recommendation: rollback.

morgan: OK blocking merge. I'll open PR 7830: revert-pack-until-full, mark it as high-priority and request fast-triage from oncall. If no :thumbsdown: within 30m I'll block the original merge.

sam: Thanks for the quick triage. Once revert PR is up, can we run a canary that keeps scoring change but reverts packing so we can keep the non-packing improvements?

morgan: Yep that's the plan — split the changes, run targeted canaries.

ryan: I'll help with bench runs and add extended flamegraphs.

morgan: Awesome. Blocking merge now. Please react if you want to unblock sooner.

(End of thread)
